info.title: Auth API
info.description:
# Overview

Auth API is a webhook that allows clients to participate in the authorization
decision making process.

SoFi Tech Solutions receives authorizaton requests for transactions,
and uses various criteria for deciding whether to approve or deny the
request (correct PIN, sufficient funds, etc.). Near the end of the authorization
request processing, we send a webhook message to your system, providing 
information about the authorization request (including how we plan to
handle the request); you can respond with how you would like the
authorization request to be processed.

# Versions
There are currently two supported versions of the Auth API - v2.0 and v3.0. The main
difference is that v3.0 provides additional details regarding response codes.
New integrations use v3.0.

# Security

You should use HTTPS for your Auth API webhook to ensure fundamental
security is in place.

SoFi Tech Solutions will use a JSON Web Token (JWT) for authenticating with your webhook. 
A shared secret will be used for encoding and decoding the token.
The payload will have the following claims:
* `iat` - Issued At
* `exp` - Expiration Time
* `iss` - "galileo"

The token will be created using the following Python code:
```python
import jwt
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
payload = {
    'exp': datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=5),
    'iat': datetime.utcnow(),
    'iss': 'galileo'
}
token = jwt.encode(payload, secret, algorithm='HS256')
```

where `secret` is the shared secret.

The token will be placed in the Authorization header field.

## Security Example

Here is the header value for `exp = 1534274886` and `iat = 1534274881`:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJnYWxpbGVvIiwiaWF0IjoxNTM0Mjc0ODgxLCJleHAiOjE1MzQyNzQ4ODZ9.1xUk4iNFGWLo01MyJUHXRlyrNlzwPvDMSXpN38TrblU
```

# Paths

You provide a base URL, hosted by a server in the client's system.
We will invoke your webhook at the `/Authorization` endpoint.

# Examples

* Override the response code
  * SoFi Tech Solutions receives an authorization request and plans to approve it
    (the account has sufficient funds, and so forth).
  * We invoke the your Auth API webhook to see if you
    want to modify the processing.
  * You see that the transaction amount is above a limit, so you indicate that
    the transaction should be declined with code `"61"` (`Exceeds Amount Limit`).
* You maintain your own balance
  * For some products, you may maintain the balance instead of
    SoFi Tech Solutions.
  * When we get a balance inquiry, we will invoke your
    Auth API webhook.
  * You can respond with the balance available, in the
    `available_balance` field.
* Client initiates transfer
  * Suppose SoFi Tech Solutions receives an authorization request, and the cardholder has
    insufficient funds; we are ready to decline the request.
  * But before we do, we invoke your Auth API webhook.
  * You see that the account has insufficient funds, so you initiate
    a transfer by sending back the `transfer_prn` and `transfer_amount`.
  * After the transfer, the cardholder has sufficient funds, so we
    approve the authorization.

servers.description: You will provide the base URL you would like to use for Auth API. The endpoint should use HTTPS.

post.description: With the Auth API 2.0 webhook, you can participate in authorization decisions. For this webhook there is only one verb: `POST`. SoFi Tech Solutions sends information about the authorization request in the body of the HTTP request, in JSON. Your decision should be in the body of the HTTP response. In the authorization information that we send, the `response_code` is the current response code to be returned to the merchant, unless you override it. Use the `response_code` field in the HTTP response body to override the authorization response code, as desired. See the Authorization Controller API guide for more information. > 📘 About the field properties > > SoFi Tech Solutions initializes the webhook payload by setting all fields to `null`. As values come in with the ISO 8583 authorization request, we populate the respective payload fields with the data the network sends, which can include empty strings (`" "`). This documentation shows the field properties (data type, nullability, required) that are most likely. However, variations by network and transaction type mean that a few of the values passed in the webhook payload can vary from what is shown here.

parameters.name: X-Request-ID
parameters.description: A unique identifier for the HTTP request.

auth_type.description:
All transactions are grouped into three basic message types:
* `Auth` — Authorization request. MTI x1xx (authorization or preauthorization over credit rails or preauthorization over debit rails) or x2xx (authorization over debit rails).
* `Advice` — Notification of a completed transaction. MTI xx2x. Only a `00` response code is permitted.
* `Reversal` — A reversal of a previous authorization. MTI x4xx. May or may not reference the previous authorization.

transaction_type.description:
The transaction type indicates at a lower level what kind of transaction this is.  This field is used to differentiate merchant credits, ATMs, balance inquiries, etc.
* `Preauth` — A preauthorization for an estimated amount. Often followed by a completion advice.
* `Auth` — Conventional authorization request. Also used with advices and reversals.
* `ATM` — ATM withdrawal.
* `Cash Advance` — Cash advance from a teller.
* `Balance Inquiry` — Balance inquiry from an ATM.
* `Merchant Credit` — A credited amount from a merchant. Usually does not reference a previous authorization.
* `Adjustment` — Debit adjustment, unrelated to a previous authorization. The merchant is adjusting a cardholder balance.
* `Payment` — Loading funds onto a card.
* `Tokenization` — A request to tokenize a card for use in a mobile wallet or a request from a merchant to validate a tokenized card for payment.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this authorization. 

Example: `"DHWJtI8zRjuDcgF8hru3oQ"`

timestamp.description:
Date and time when the webhook was sent by SoFi Tech Solutions.

Format is `<timestamp><timezone>`, where `timestamp` is `YYYYMMDD:HHMMSS` and `timezone` is always `MST`, which is Arizona time (GMT -0700).

Example: `"20250315:121504MST"`

subnetwork.description:
The subnetwork name. This is the same as `network` if there is no subnetwork. Possible values:

* `Visa`
* `Visa Interlink`
* `Visa PLUS`
* `Mastercard Banknet`
* `Mastercard Debit Switch`
* `Discover`
* `Allpoint`
* `Star`
* `Star MoneyPass`
* `Star Presto`
* `Pulse`

xid.description:
Internal ID for the account.

Example: `5398373`

cad.description:
System-generated ID for the card. This ID has a 1:1 relationship with the <<glossary:PAN>>.

Example: `72450868`

prn.description: Payment reference number for the account. 12 digits. Example: `"999200002022"`

product_id.description:
Product ID for the account, as provided by SoFi Tech Solutions.

Example: `2577`

program_id.description:
Program ID for the account, as provided by SoFi Tech Solutions.

Example: `566`

pan.description:
Last four digits of the <<glossary:PAN>> of the card.

Example: `"5198"`

account_status.description: Account status code. See the possible values in the Account Statuses enumeration. Example: `"N"`

card_status.description: Card status code. See the possible values in the Card Statuses enumeration. Example: `"N"`

track_expiration_date.description:
The expiration date (format: `YYMM`) that was read from the card's magnetic stripe and sent in the ISO message, if present and applicable. For example, this field will not be present for a card-not-present transaction.

Example: `"2103"`

merchant_supplied_expiration_date.description:
The expiration date (format: `YYMM`) supplied by the merchant, if present and applicable.


Example: `"2103"`

amounts.description:
The amounts are always unsigned. To calculate the sign for an amount, start with a factor of –1, and then apply another factor of –1 for each of the following criteria:
* `"auth_type": "Reversal"`
* `"transaction_type": "Merchant Credit"`
* `"transaction_type": "Payment"`

Amount fields may not display a numeric value for non-active cards. Instead, the string `"none"` could be displayed.

currency.description:
The currency code for the amounts, unless otherwise indicated. This is the currency of the cardholder account. ISO 4217 Numeric Currency Code. 3 digits.

Example: `"840"`

trans_amount.description:
Transaction amount. Full amount of the authorization request, including upcharges and fees and after any currency conversion is performed.

Example: `"12.40"`

partial_amount.description:
If `partial_supported: true` and `response_code` is `10` or `87`, this is the amount of the partial approval.

Example: `"10.00"`

cashback_amount.description:
Cashback amount requested. This amount is included in `trans_amount`.

Example: `"5.00"`

fee_amount.description:
Amount of any fees. This amount is included in `trans_amount`.

Example: `"1.50"`

available_funds.description: The card's available balance before this transaction is applied. If this authorization request is approved, the card's available balance is affected within a few milliseconds after the approval is sent to the network. Keep in mind that this is the available balance known to SoFi Tech Solutions—if you are the system of record for your program, refer to your records to determine whether the account has sufficient funds. Example: `100.00`

amt_til_limit.description:
Amount remaining before `nearest_limit` is reached.

Example: `502.80`

nearest_limit.description:
The name of the first limit that would be reached if a partial authorization or denied authorization is overridden via the `override_limit` field. This field is present only when the limit would be reached in overriding the authorization.

Example: `"PCL Daily Limit"`

local_currency.description:
ISO 4217 numeric currency code for `local_currency_amount`, which is the currency at the point of sale. 3 digits.

Example: `"124"`

local_currency_amount.description:
Amount of the request in the currency at the point of sale. Upcharges and fees are not included.

Example: `"21.00"`

settle_currency.description: ISO 4217 numeric currency code for `settlement_currency_amount`. To understand what a settlement currency is, see Multicurrency BINs. 3 digits. Example: `"978"`

settle_currency_amount.description:
Amount of the request in the settlement currency. Upcharges and fees are not included.


Example: `"17.00"`

billing_currency.description:
ISO 4217 numeric currency code for `billing_currency_amount`.

Example: `840`

billing_currency_amount.description:
The amount of the transaction in the billing currency, which is the currency of the card account.

Example: `"12.40"`

local_surcharge_amt.description:
The surcharge amount in the currency at the point of sale.

Example: `"0.50"`

settle_surcharge_amt.description:
The surcharge amount in the settlement currency.

Example: `"0.75"`

settle_exchange_rate.description:
The factor used to convert from the local request amount to the settlement amount. The string has the pattern `<shift digit><exchange rate digits>`. The first digit specifies how many places from the right the decimal is moved. For example, `69985022` translates to an exchange rate of 9.985022%.

Example: `"69985022"`

exchange_rate.description:
The factor used to convert from the local request amount to the billing amount. The string has the pattern `<shift digit><exchange rate digits>`. The first digit specifies how many places from the right the decimal is moved. For example, `69985022` translates to an exchange rate of 9.985022%.

Example: `"65991234"`

upcharge_amount.description:
The upcharge amount, which is included in `trans_amount`.

Example: `"75.00"`

mcc.description:
Merchant category code. This value does not include leading zeros.

Example: `5992`

digital_commerce_data.description: _Mastercard only_. Contains data regarding a digital commerce transaction. Derived from DE048SE48. See Digital Commerce Solutions Indicators for more information.

entity_type_name.description:
SF3. The check-in entity type and entity name.

Example: `"202010030220"`

domain_id.description:
SF1. The entity responsible for populating the other fields in this object.

Example: `"01"`

program_id.description:
SF2. The specific digital commerce program.
          

Example: `"01"`

checkin_method.description:
SF4. The methods that a check-in entity applies to validate cardholder presence. **Required** when `program_id: 04`.

Example: `" "`

terminal_id.description:
The ID for the device that acquired the card information.

Example: `"A1Z23B99"`

merchant_id.description:
The merchant ID, as assigned by the network.

Example: `"39AJKEO30634KVN3"`

merchant_description.description:
The merchant description.

Example: `"123 WIDGETS MERCHANT BEVERLY HILLS CA"`

merchant_country.description:
ISO 3166-1 country code for the country where the merchant is located. 3 digits.

Example: `"840"`

merchant_postal_code.description:
Postal code, nine characters. Left-justified and padded with zeros. If there are nine zeros, then no postal code was provided.

Example: `"902100000"`

merchant_state.description:
Two-letter state or provincial designator for the merchant's location.

Example: `"NV"`

terminal_network.description:
Network to which the terminal belongs, Possible values are `VPA` (Visa PLUS Alliance), `Allpoint`, or `None` (another network). If you are not configured to receive this data, the value will always be `None`.


Example: `"VPA"`

mti.description: Message-type indicator, as defined by ISO 8583. See Message types in the _Authorization Controller API_ guide. Example: `"0200"`

recurring.description:
Whether a transaction is recurring: `Y` or `N`.

Example: `"N"`

cardholder_present.description:
Whether the physical card was present at the point of sale: `Y` or `N`.

Example: `"Y"`

transaction_initiator_code.description: *Mastercard only.* Whether the transaction was initiated by the cardholder or the merchant. Populated only when DE048 subfield 22 is present in the authorization request. See CIT and MIT Indicators for more information. Example: `"M101"`

is_advance_payment.description: _Visa only_. Field 126 SE 13. Whether the transaction is an advance payment, meaning that the merchant secures the payment before the goods or services are available.

cvv1.description:
Result of <<glossary:CVV>>1 validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

cvv2.description:
Result of CVV2 validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

cvv3.description:
Result of CVV3 validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

pin.description:
Result of PIN validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Verified
* `F` — Failed
* `L` — Locked
* `M` — PIN not set
* `B` — Blocked
* `N` — No PIN was passed

arqc.description:
Result of validating the authorization request cryptogram for an EMV chip. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

offline_pin.description:
Result of validating the offline PIN. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present
* `E` — Offline PIN attempts exceeded
* `P` — Ignored due to risk params

avs_result.description: Result of the <> check. See AVS Codes for valid values. Example: `"Y"`

aav.description:
Result of validating the <<glossary:AAV>>/<<glossary:CAVV>>. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

avs_data.description: When the authorization includes an <<glossary:AVS>> request, this object contains the data that SoFi Tech Solutions used to calculate the AVS response.

zip.description:
Postal code provided by the cardholder.

Example: `"84121"`

address.description:
Numbers in the first address line, provided by the cardholder.

Example: `"1235"`

international.description: Whether this is an international transaction.

response_code.description: Authorization response code, which specifies whether a transaction is approved or denied. See the Authorization Response Codes enumeration for possible values. Example: `"05"`

auth_id.description: System-generated ID for the authorization. Use this ID to track the transaction throughout the system. For an explanation of how these IDs are generated, see Authorization identifiers in the _Transaction IDs_ guide. Example: `13371854`

partial_supported.description: Whether the merchant supports partial authorizations.

stip.description: This object is present when a <> transaction is processed by the network. See Stand-in processing in the _Authorization Controller API_ guide for more information.

detail.description: Advice reason code relayed from the network, which provides information on the STIP transaction. See Advice Reason Codes for valid values. Example: `"4000000"` or `"9020"`

stip_decision.description: The Authorization Response Code that was returned to the merchant by the STIP process. Example: `"00"`

additional_detail.description: More information about the STIP transaction. See STIP Additional Detail for valid values. Example: `"000003"`

is_stip_denial.description:
Whether the transaction was denied by the STIP process: `N` (approved). Denied STIP transactions do not trigger an Auth API message.

Example: `"N"`

incremental_auth.description: If this authorization is part of an an incremental sequence, this field is `true` and `original_id` contains the `auth_id` of the previous authorization in the sequence.

entry_type.description: Method of entering the <>, also known as <> entry mode. See DE022 Codes to correlate with the numerical values. Possible values: * `Card Not Present` — Online, mail order or telephone order * `Card On File` — _Mastercard only._ Card number is kept on file * `E-Commerce` — _Mastercard only._ The card was used on an ecommerce site * `EMV Chip` — The card has an EMV chip that was inserted in an EMV slot * `EMV Contactless` — Contactless transaction with EMV chip card * `EMV Fallback` — Unable to use the EMV chip: fallback to magstripe * `Magnetic Stripe` — The magnetic stripe was read * `Contactless` — Contactless transaction with magstripe card * `Manual` — Manually entered information * `Other` — None of the above

pin_entry_capability.description: Condition of the PIN pad at the point of sale. See DE022 Codes to correlate with the numerical values. Possible values: * `Capable` — Terminal has PIN-entry capability * `Incapable` — Terminal has no PIN-entry capability * `Inoperative` — Terminal has PIN-entry capability but it is not working * `Other` — Unknown PIN-entry capability, or not applicable.

payment_info.description: When `transaction_type` is `Payment`, the name of the sender and fund source, if provided in the request.

sender_name.description:
Name of the sender of the payment.

Example: `"John Doe"`.

fund_source.description:
Source of the payment.

Example: `"Visa Prepaid"`.

original_id.description:
The `auth_id` of a previous authorization that is linked to this authorization. For reversals or completions, this is the `auth_id` of the authorization that is being reversed or completed. For incremental sequences, this is the `auth_id` of the previous authorization in the sequence.

Example: `13663253`

risk_score.description:
The risk score provided by the network. Mastercard range: 0–999, Visa range: 01–99. Higher values indicate higher risk. Product settings determine whether the threshold was exceeded.

Example: `"23"`

token_type.description:
If this is a tokenized transaction, its type. Possible values:
* `Apple Inc`
* `Google Inc.`
* `Masterpass`
* `Merchant`
* `Microsoft`
* `Samsung Corporation`
* `Visa Checkout`

rules_denied.description:
Valid only when using our fraud-rules engine. List of fraud rules that caused a decline. Set the RULAP product parameter to receive these rules.

Example: `["hr_crypto:DENY", "intl_cnp_ecom:DENY"]`

rules_warned.description:
Valid only when using our fraud-rules engine. List of fraud rules that caused a warning. Set the RULAP product parameter to receive these rules.

Example: `["dom_cp:WARN"]`

response_code_list.description: List of response codes that SoFi Tech Solutions has computed. This list does not contain `"00"`. May be empty. Example: `["05", "51"]`.

items.description: Authorization response code, which specifies whether a transaction is approved or denied. See the Authorization Response Codes enumeration for possible values. Example: `"05"`

bai.description: Business application identifier. _Visa only._ See the Business Application Identifier enumeration for possible values. Example: `"FD"`

risk_code.description:
_Mastercard only_. Fraud reason code. Indicates the key factors that influenced the value in `risk_score`.

Example: `"58"`

ecommerce.description: This object contains information related to <> authentication, if the website supported 3DS. Included in this information is the result of validating the <> for Mastercard or the <> for Visa. For detailed information about these fields, refer to The ecommerce object in the _3-D Secure Access Control Server_ guide.

is_ecommerce.description: Whether the transaction took place on a website that supports 3DS.

raw_eci.description:
The electronic commerce indicator (ECI) that is sent in the authorization request.

Example: `"212"`

merchant_asserts_data_protection.description: Whether the merchant or acquirer claims that the connection between the ecommerce site and the cardholder was encrypted.

merchant_asserts_authentication_attempte.description: Whether the merchant or acquirer claims that 3DS authentication was attempted.

merchant_asserts_authenticated.description: Whether the merchant or acquirer claims that the 3DS authentication was successful.

merchant_authentication_assertions_valid.description: Validation results of the merchant's assertions.

cavv_result_code.description: _Visa only_. A code that indicates the outcome of CAVV validation. See CAVV Result Code for valid values. Example: `"B"`

eligible_for_balance_return.description: Whether the cardholder's balance can be returned. This field is always `true` when `transaction_type: Balance Inquiry`. See Balance-inquiry responses in the _Authorization Controller API_ guide for information on returning balances in the response to this message.

emv.description: Additional EMV information. Also see EMV entry types under `entry_type` and EMV-related fields under `validation_results`.

is_emv.description: This field is `true` if the `entry_type` is `EMV Chip` or `EMV Contactless`. When this value is `true`, the remaining fields below will be present, although they may be only partially populated, depending on the card network or EMV entry type.

brand.description:
Type of EMV. Possible values:
* `visa`
* `mastercard`
* `discover`

The card network may not match the EMV brand. For example, Visa EMV technology can be used on a card whose BIN is serviced through Allpoint.

terminal_verification_results.description:
This object interprets the status bits sent by the payment terminal, based on what happened during the transaction, such as whether the cardholder entered a valid PIN. Selected bits of the TVR have been separated out into the Boolean fields below.

Use these fields with caution: There can be inconsistencies between different networks, and some bits are not applicable for certain entry types such as `EMV Contactless`. For example, Discover states that byte 3, bits 4 and 5 should be ignored for contactless transactions.

raw.description:
The raw TVR (as a hex string) that was received in the ISO 8583 message, if present. If not present this field is null and the remaining fields in the `terminal_verification_results` object will not be present.

Example: `"0000000000"`

online_pin_entered.description: _Byte 3, bit 3._ Whether a PIN is being sent in the ISO message for validation instead of using offline validation (where the EMV chip on the card validates the PIN).

pin_required_pad_pres_but_no_pin_entered.description: _Byte 3, bit 4._ Whether the merchant or cardholder chose to bypass PIN entry, and the PIN pad was operational.

pin_required_no_pad_or_bad_pad.description: _Byte 3, bit 5._ Whether a PIN was required but there was no PIN pad, or the PIN pad wasn't working.

pin_try_limit_exceeded.description: _Byte 3, bit 6._ Whether the PIN-try limit was exceeded. For example, the terminal read the PIN-try counter on the chip and it was zero.

cardholder_verification_not_successful.description: _Byte 3, bit 8._ Whether the terminal indicates that cardholder verification was not successful.

version.description:
Auth API version of this webhook.

Example: `"2.0"`

iias_info.description: _Visa only_. Present when the items or services being purchased include eligible medical expenses. Derived from Field 54 and Field 62. This object is present only when <> information is included with the authorization request. For more information, see IIAS fields in the _Auth API Field Detail_ guide.

iias_indicator.description:
`M` indicates that the card is an <<glossary:FSA>>, <<glossary:HRA>>, or <<glossary:HSA>> card. Field 62.4.

Example: `"M"`

merchant_verification_value.description:
IIAS merchant verification value for the <<glossary:SIGIS>>-certified merchant location. Field 62.20.

Example: `"1234560000"`

qualified_healthcare_products_total.description:
Amount of `trans_amount` that qualifies as a healthcare product or service. Field 54, amount type 4S.

Example: `"64.87"`

rx_total.description:
Amount that is prescription medication. Field 54, amount type 4U.

Example: `"64.87"`

vision_total.description:
Amount that is vision-related. Field 54, amount type 4V.

Example: `"0.00"`

clinic_total.description:
Amount that is a clinic visit. Field 54, amount type 4W.

Example: `"0.00"`

dental_total.description:
Amount that is dental-related. Field 54, amount type 4X.

Example: `"0.00"`

advanced_auth_api_fields.description: Selected subfields parsed from the ISO 8583 message. These fields are sent only when ADVAF is set and only by arrangement with SoFi Tech Solutions. See Advanced Auth API Fields for more information. Example: `"advanced_auth_api_fields": {"61": {"subfield 1": , "subfield 2": }}`

tar_info.description: Tokenization authorization request (TAR) data is provided by the network during mobile wallet provisioning. The following are the subfields in a tokenization authorization request. Note the distinctions between Mastercard and Visa networks. For enhanced provisioning security based on some of these fields, see Enhanced provisioning security in _Setup for Mobile Wallets_. If you do not receive this data for provisioning approved BINs, contact SoFi Tech Solutions for assistance.

correlation_id.description:
_Mastercard only._ Identifier assigned that can be used by the issuer to associate related tokenization requests and notification messages. 14 alphanumeric characters.

Example: `"D0002688797932"`

pan_source.description:
For Mastercard, this field identifies the method by which the cardholder is attempting to tokenize a PAN.
- `1` — Card on file
- `2` — Card added manually
- `3` — Card added via application


For Visa, this tag, if present, identifies whether it’s push provisioning.
- `01` — Key entered
- `02` — On file
- `03` — Mobile banking application
- `04` — Token
- `05` — Chip dip
- `06` — Contactless

If the value is `03`, then it is push provisioning.

payment_app_instance_id.description:
_Mastercard only._ Identifier associated with the payment application instance installed onto the customer's device. 48 alphanumeric characters.

Example: `"tSnaYXYaTSkz7DoGPz_wvVLhieie4lyhMPuMrvXx4kdAwkgV"`

device_ip.description:
For Mastercard, this field is the variable-length IP address. Each octet of the IP address is converted to hex and joined into one string, with the order maintained. 8 alphanumeric characters.

Example: `"83BF5B74"`

For Visa, this field contains the IP address of the device at the time of the provisioning request. 15 characters maximum.

Example: `"255.255.255.255"`

acc_id_hash.description:
_Mastercard only._ Contains the customer’s account ID associated with the wallet provider as a PBKDF2 hash. This account ID is typically the email address. The PBKDF2 function is performed using 10 iterations, a salt, and the lowercase account ID as the password. The salt is calculated by taking the lowercase UTF-8 bytes from the account ID and performing a SHA-256 hash operation.

**Example**:
Input (Password): `csharp@walletprovider.com`
Salt: `"41404d1bca85ddb59ab21466e277ac1ac5f61470be120c82a21b1e45b5248123"`
Count: `10`
Output: `"7098014b646d44c6f3b454c5d54f7a32b3b46e2b0c8e2367f3e5307e3036dfe6"`

cardholder_name.description:
_Mastercard only._ Contains the name of the cardholder. The format is represented in one of these two formats:
- LASTNAME/FIRSTNAME with the names delimited by a slash `/`.

Example: `"SMITH/JOE"`
- FIRSTNAME LASTNAME.

Example: `"JOE SMITH"`

27 characters maximum. If the cardholder’s name is longer than 27 positions, the data is truncated.

tokenization_recommendation.description:
The tokenization decision suggested by the wallet provider.

For Mastercard, possible values are:
- `0` — Decline
- `1` — Approve
- `2` — Requires additional authentication

For Visa, possible values are:
- `0` — Unconditionally approved
- `1` — Conditionally approved with further cardholder verification
- `2` — Not approved

tokenization_recommendation_standard_ver.description:
The version of the standards the wallet provider is using to determine the suggested tokenization recommendation.

- For Mastercard, this value is 2 digits.

Example: `"01"`
- For Visa, this value is a decimal value.

Example: `"0002.00"`

device_score.description:
The score assigned by the wallet provider for the device. The score is returned as a value between `1` and `5`, with `5` being most trusted.

Example: `5`

account_score.description:
_Mastercard only._ Score assigned by the wallet provider for the <<glossary:PAN>>. Value between`1` and `5`, with `5` being most trusted.

Example: `5`

active_tokens.description:
_Mastercard only._ Number of existing, active tokens for the PAN, excluding card-on-file tokens. Space-filled when the requested token is digitized to a server.

Example: `"08"`

tokenization_recommendation_reason_code.description: Indicates the specific reason the wallet provider is suggesting the tokenization recommendation. For Mastercard, the data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, whereby each bit corresponds to a specific reason code. If the wallet provider returns no reason, this field will contain spaces. See the possible values for Visa in the Tokenization Recommendation Reason Codes. Example: `"008011"`

tokenization_recommendation_reason_codes.description: _Mastercard only._ Indicates the specific reason the wallet provider is suggesting the tokenization recommendation. This field shows the interpretation of the hex-encoded bitmap in the `tokenization_recommendation_reason_code` field for Mastercard. See the possible values for this field in the Tokenization Recommendation Reason Codes. Example: `"08" `

location.description:
Latitude and longitude points where the cardholder's device was located at the time the tokenization was attempted.

- For Mastercard. The decimal latitude and longitude values, converted to hexadecimal.

Example: `"2F197A2E1"`
- For Visa, when available, the latitude and longitude points are provided with up to 4 digits of precision or rounded to a less-granular level.

Example: `"+39.13/-77.55"`

last_four_digits.description:
_Mastercard only._ Last four digits of the cardholder's mobile phone number associated with the active wallet.

Example: `"0885"`

token_type.description:
The type of requested token.
- `C` — Mastercard cloud-based payments
- `F` — Card on file
- `S` — Embedded secure element
- `H` — <<glossary:VTS>> cloud token

consumer_identifier.description: _Mastercard only._ Unique identifier for each cardholder, which must be verified by the financial institution before a cardholder can add their credentials to the payment-enabled device. Default: blank.

device_type.description:
_Visa only._ Device type value.
- `00` — Unknown
- `01` — Mobile phone
- `02` — Tablet
- `03` — Watch
- `04` — Mobile phone or tablet
- `05` — Personal computer

device_language.description:
_Visa only._ Language used by the cardholder’s device. 3 characters maximum.

Example: `"eng"` for English.

device_id.description:
_Visa only._ The device ID. 48 characters maximum.

Example: `"MTgwOTIxMTQzMjAwMTA0LUh0"`

device_number.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the device number, or the full or partial telephone number, when available. Provided by the Visa network.

Example: `"15127717396"`

device_name.description:
_Visa only._ The name of the device given by the cardholder. 16 characters maximum. Value is truncated when longer than maximum length.

Example: `"Work Phone"`

account_id.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the wallet account ID.

Example: `"eg2t6TyJQ2G8NIraaCypzg"`

account_email_addr.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the hashed full email address for the cardholder account that was sent by the wallet provider.

Example: `"\xc1_\xf8\xc8_/\xd1%%\x06\xc4?_"`

visa_token_score.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the Visa Token Score associated with a token. Scores range from 01-99, with higher values indicating higher risk. `00` indicates a token was not scored.
Example: `"01"`

fleet_info.description: Information that is provided for cards with fleet-card BINs, which are Mastercard only. See Fleet Cards for more information.

fleet_prompt_data.description:
Contains occurrences of the prompt code read from a card chip. There can be up to 5 prompt codes. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for the full list.

Example: `002` (vehicle number)

merchant_override_indicator.description: Indicates if the merchant point-of-sale supports the fleet spend control override capability: `0` (does not support) or `1` (supports)

control_override_items.description: Provides merchants with information, on a transaction basis, to override purchase restrictions to allow products to be purchased that may not have otherwise been allowed. Only to be populated when DE106SE2 contains the value `1`, indicating that the merchant point-of-sale supports the fleet spend-control override capability.

fuel_info.description:
Contains item-level detail information of the motor fuel product(s) purchased at the POS (3 digit code). Can have up to 3 subfields. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for the full list.

Example: `036` (racing fuel)

non_fuel_info.description:
Contains item-level detail information of the non-fuel product(s) purchased at the POS. Can have up to 12 subfields. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for the full list.

Example: `102` (car wash)

aifi_fields.description: _Colombia only_. Information related to ATM issuer-fee inquiries.

issuer_fee_inquiry_indicator.description: Contains `"01"` to indicate issuer-fee inquiry request. DE112SE035.

pos_transaction_status.description: Contains `"8"` to indicate account-status inquiry (ASI) service. DE061SF7.

issuer_fee_amt.description:
Amount of the ATD (domestic ATM) fee. This amount is displayed to the cardholder as the issuer fee. DE112SE036.

Example: `"15000.00"`

merchant_advice_code.description: _Mastercard only._ Contains the supported merchant advice code (MAC), if applicable: `03`, `40`, `41`, or `43`. The GMACD parameter must be set to `Y` to enable MAC decisioning.

fraud_results.description: _Mastercard only_. Contains the results from the Mastercard Fraud Rule Management Service. If you subscribe to this service, ask SoFi Tech Solutions to enable this object. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for DE048SE56 to interpret the values.

fraud_scoring_data.description: _Mastercard only._ DE048SE75. Contains the results from Mastercard's Expert Monitoring, Fraud Scoring Service, or Decision Intelligence (DI) service. If you subscribe to any of these services, ask SoFi Tech Solutions to enable this object. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for your service to interpret the values.

risk_assessment_score.description:
Mastercard Decision Intelligence (DI) score ranging from `0-999`.

Example: `"089"`

risk_assessment_score_reason_code.description:
Fraud reason code. Indicates the key factors that influenced the value in `risk_assessment_score`.

Example: `"64"`

real_time_fraud_score.description:
The Fraud Rule Manager Service provides the rule-adjusted score of `000-999`, where `000` indicates the least likely fraudulent transaction and `999` indicates the most likely fraudulent transaction.

Example: `"089"`

real_time_fraud_score_reason_code_1.description:
An alphanumeric reason code that identifies the data used to derive the `real_time_fraud_score`.

Example: `"64"`

real_time_fraud_score_reason_code_2.description:
An alphanumeric reason code that identifies the data used to derive the `real_time_fraud_score`.

Example: `"00"`

digital_payment_data.description: _Mastercard only._ DE104SE4. Contains the results from Mastercard's Token Authentication Framework (TAF) program. If you subscribe to Mastercard's Expert Monitoring, Fraud Scoring Service, or Decision Intelligence (DI) service, ask SoFi Tech Solutions to enable this object to use for decisioning. Consult the documentation from Mastercard on DE104 Subelement 004 to interpret the values.

digital_service_provider.description:
Identifies the entity that authenticated the transaction. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for a complete list of values for DE104SE4SF1.

Example: `"001005A0010"`

digital_authentication_data.description:
Confirms that the transaction was fully authenticated, and identifies the authentication method used. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for a complete list of values for DE104SE5SF1.

Example:`"0010054TRID00200500000"`

latest_incremental_id.description:
The `auth_id` of the previous authorization in an incremental sequence when `incremental_auth: true`. This field contains the same information as `original_id` and is present only by request.

Example: `13371854`

original_incremental_id.description:
The `auth_id` of the first authorization in an incremental sequence when `incremental_auth: true`. This field is present only by request.

Example: `13369203`

account_attack_intelligence_score.description:
_Visa only_. A score for <<glossary:CNP>> transactions to evaluate risk of enumeration attacks. Field 104, Dataset 5B, Tag 85. Valid values are `01-99` or null. Lower scores mean less risk.

Example: `"24"`

relay_resistance_protocol_data.description: _Mastercard only_. DE048SE71. For tokenized (mobile wallet), contactless transactions, this is information captured at the terminal related to the possibility of relay attacks. For valid values, see Relay Resistance Protocol Data.

on_behalf_service.description:
The type of service performed on the transaction.

Example: `"51"`

result_1.description:
The first result from the on-behalf service.

Example: `"A"`

result_2.description:
The second result from the on-behalf service, if any.

Example: `"K"`

service_processing_type.description: _Visa only_. Service processing type for scheduled, deferred <>s. See Service Processing Types for valid values. Field 104 Dataset 57 Tag 80. Example: `"03"`

managed_service_indicator.description:
Whether this is a managed-service transaction. Tag 82.

Example: `"Y"`

agreement_type.description:
The type of managed service that was provided for this transaction. Consult the documentation from Visa for valid values. Tag C1. Max 4 char.

Example: `"1234"`

is_in_person_tap_transaction.description: _Visa only_. Whether this is a direct in-person tap transaction. Applies only to <<glossary:OCT>>s and <<glossary:AFT>>s. Field 34.

vdcap_info.description: _Visa only_. <<glossary:VDCAP>> information from Field 34, Field 56, and Field 111.

authentication_program.description: Indicates which authentication solution or data-sharing solution was used to process the transaction. See VDCAP Info for valid values. Field 34 Dataset 01 Tag C0. Example: `"01"`

consumer_device_ip_address.description:
External IP address that is the device public IP address used by the 3DS requestor application when it connects to the 3DS requestor environment. Field 34 Dataset 01 Tag 92.

Example: `"172.16.22.52"`

applied_special_service.description:
Indicates whether the merchant has used the eligible authentication or data-sharing method and provided the required data elements. Visa sends `1` (<<glossary:VDCAP>>) if all the conditions are met. Field 111 Dataset 56 Tag 89.

Example: `"1"`

other_phone_number.description:
A phone number belonging to the cardholder. Field 56 Dataset 02 Tag 83. Max 16 char.

Example: `"8015552333"`

browser_ip_address.description:
3DS browser IP address. Field 34 Dataset 01 Tag 89.

Example `"10.0.45.66"`

other_email_address.description:
An email address belonging to the cardholder. Field 56 Dataset 02 Tag 86. Max 99 char.

Example: `"3dsuser@exampledomain.com"`

device_id.description:
Unique identifier associated with the cardholder device. Field 34 Dataset 06 Tag 86. Max 64 char.

Example: `"device000"`

credit_info.description: Contains information related to credit accounts.

credit_card_balance.description:
The outstanding balance on a credit account. This value can be interpreted as being accurate as of the `opentobuy_ts`.

Example: "-249.51"

opentobuy_ts.description:
Date and time when when the `credit_card_balance` was last captured. Format is YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.ssssss and timezone is always `MST`, which is Arizona time (GMT -0700).

Example: `"2025-03-17 14:06:50.243654"`

mastercard_transaction_id_data.description: _Mastercard only_. Derived from DE105, Multi-Use Transaction Identification Data. Contains the <<glossary:TLID>>, which is globally unique in a distributed environment and used as a single unique reference to perform matching and linking of all message activity

tlid.description: DE105SE1. Transaction link identifier. A unique ID that Mastercard generates for each original transaction. Example: `"aabb112233445566"`

economically_related_tlid.description: DE105SE2. The Mastercard-generated TLID from an economically related independent transaction that a customer retains and returns in subsequent economically related transactions.

lifecycle_tlid_validation_data.description: Data relative to the TLID lifecycle.

action_indicator.description:
DE105SE3SF1. Indicates whether Mastercard modified the `tlid`, either because the customer did not provide a TLID in a lifecycle-linking scenario, or the TLID was unmatched. Possible values:
- `1` — Mastercard populated `tlid` with the original message TLID. The customer did not submit a lifecycle message with a TLID, and so `customer_provided_tlid` will not be populated.
- `2` — Mastercard populated `tlid` with the original lifecycle message TLID. The customer submitted the lifecycle message with a TLID value that did not match the original message. Mastercard moved the customer-provided TLID value to `customer_provided_tlid`.
- `3` — Mastercard generated a new TLID value for `tlid`. Mastercard was unable to match this lifecycle message to any original message. If the customer submitted this transaction with a TLID value, Mastercard moved the customer-provided TLID value to `customer_provided_tlid`.

customer_provided_tlid.description: DE105SE3SF2. Contains the customer-provided TLID value from DE105SE1 (`tlid`) when Mastercard is unable to confirm the validity of that customer-provided TLID value.

200.description: Use the fields in this schema to respond with your decision plus any instructions for SoFi Tech Solutions.

response_code.description: Authorization response code, which specifies whether a transaction is approved or denied. See the Authorization Response Codes enumeration for possible values. Example: `"05"`

avs_response.description: Use this field to override `avs_result`, if you believe `avs_result` is wrong. See AVS Codes for valid values. Example: `"Y"`

override_limit.description: Use this field to override authorization limits, if permitted. If this field is `true` then any limits that would be reached are overridden. Example: `true`

partial_amount.description: If `response_code` indicates a partial approval (`10` or `87`), this is the partial amount to approve. Example: `5.00`

transfer_prn.description: If you want to perform a transfer to cover a lack of funds, this is the PRN of the account to supply the funds. Example: `"155200002717"`

transfer_amount.description: The amount to transfer from the `transfer_prn` to the cardholder account. Example: `20.00`

source_transfer_type.description: The transaction type for the adjustment on the source account in `transfer_prn`. Use the value that SoFi Tech Solutions supplied. Case sensitive. Default: `pc`. Example: `"lm"`

dest_transfer_type.description: The transaction type for the adjustment to the cardholder account. Use the value that SoFi Tech Solutions supplied. Case sensitive. Default: `PC` Example: `"LM"`

available_balance.description: If `eligible_for_balance_return: true` AND you hold the ledger for the card account, populate this field with the card account's available balance to spend _before_ the transaction is performed. Otherwise, SoFi Tech Solutions sends the balance it has in the response message. The amount should be in the account currency. (The card networks will perform currency conversion as needed.) Example: `250.00`

savings_balance.description: If `eligible_for_balance_return: true` AND you hold the ledger for the cardholder's savings account, populate this field with the savings account balance in the currency of the account. Otherwise, SoFi Tech Solutions sends the balance it has in the response message. Example: `4000.00`

available_credit.description: If `eligible_for_balance_return: true` AND you hold the ledger for the cardholder's credit account, populate this field with the credit limit remaining in the currency of the account. Otherwise, SoFi Tech Solutions sends the remaining limit it has in the response message. Example: `1500.00`

merchant_advice_code.description: *Mastercard only.* Use this field to override MAC decisioning, if permitted. Leave blank if you do not wish to override the SoFi Tech Solutions MAC decision. SoFi Tech Solutions reverts to the original decision if an invalid MAC is provided. The MACO product parameter must be set to `Y` to enable overrides.

post.description: With the Auth API 3.0 webhook, you can participate in authorization decisions. For this webhook there is only one verb: `POST`. SoFi Tech Solutions sends information about the authorization request in the body of the HTTP request, in JSON. Your decision should be in the body of the HTTP response. In the authorization information that we send, the `response_code` is the current response code to be returned to the merchant, unless you override it. Use the `response_code` field in the HTTP response body to override the authorization response code, as desired. See the Authorization Controller API guide for more information. > 📘 About the field properties > > SoFi Tech Solutions initializes the webhook payload by setting all fields to `null`. As values come in with the ISO 8583 authorization request, we populate the respective payload fields with the data the network sends, which can include empty strings (`" "`). This documentation shows the field properties (data type, nullability, required) that are most likely. However, variations by network and transaction type mean that a few of the values passed in the webhook payload can vary from what is shown here. Open the Recipes below to see webhook examples that you can use for testing.

parameters.name: X-Request-ID
parameters.description: A unique identifier for the HTTP request.

auth_type.description:
All transactions are grouped into three basic message types:
* `Auth` — Authorization request. MTI x1xx (authorization or preauthorization over credit rails or preauthorization over debit rails) or x2xx (authorization over debit rails).
* `Advice` — Notification of a completed transaction. MTI xx2x. Only a `00` response code is permitted.
* `Reversal` — A reversal of a previous authorization. MTI x4xx. May or may not reference the previous authorization.

transaction_type.description:
The transaction type indicates at a lower level what kind of transaction this is.  This field is used to differentiate merchant credits, ATMs, balance inquiries, etc.
* `Preauth` — A preauthorization for an estimated amount. Often followed by a completion advice.
* `Auth` — Conventional authorization request. Also used with advices and reversals.
* `ATM` — ATM withdrawal.
* `Cash Advance` — Cash advance from a teller.
* `Balance Inquiry` — Balance inquiry from an ATM.
* `Merchant Credit` — A credited amount from a merchant. Usually does not reference a previous authorization.
* `Adjustment` — Debit adjustment, unrelated to a previous authorization. The merchant is adjusting a cardholder balance.
* `Payment` — Loading funds onto a card.
* `Tokenization` — A request to tokenize a card for use in a mobile wallet or a request from a merchant to validate a tokenized card for payment.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this authorization. 

Example: `"DHWJtI8zRjuDcgF8hru3oQ"`

timestamp.description:
Date and time when the webhook was sent by SoFi Tech Solutions.

Format is `<timestamp><timezone>`, where `timestamp` is `YYYYMMDD:HHMMSS` and `timezone` is always `MST`, which is Arizona time (GMT -0700).

Example: `"20250315:121504MST"`

subnetwork.description:
The subnetwork name. This is the same as `network` if there is no subnetwork. Possible values:

* `Visa`
* `Visa Interlink`
* `Visa PLUS`
* `Mastercard Banknet`
* `Mastercard Debit Switch`
* `Discover`
* `Allpoint`
* `Star`
* `Star MoneyPass`
* `Star Presto`
* `Pulse`

xid.description:
Internal ID for the account.

Example: `5398373`

cad.description:
System-generated ID for the card. This ID has a 1:1 relationship with the <<glossary:PAN>>.

Example: `72450868`

prn.description: Payment reference number for the account. 12 digits. Example: `"999200002022"`

product_id.description:
Product ID for the account, as provided by SoFi Tech Solutions.

Example: `2577`

program_id.description:
Program ID for the account, as provided by SoFi Tech Solutions.

Example: `566`

pan.description:
Last four digits of the <<glossary:PAN>> of the card.

Example: `"5198"`

account_status.description: Account status code. See the possible values in the Account Statuses enumeration. Example: `"N"`

card_status.description: Card status code. See the possible values in the Card Statuses enumeration. Example: `"N"`

track_expiration_date.description:
The expiration date (format: `YYMM`) that was read from the card's magnetic stripe and sent in the ISO message, if present and applicable. For example, this field will not be present for a card-not-present transaction.

Example: `"2103"`

merchant_supplied_expiration_date.description:
The expiration date (format: `YYMM`) supplied by the merchant, if present and applicable.


Example: `"2103"`

amounts.description:
The amounts are always unsigned. To calculate the sign for an amount, start with a factor of –1, and then apply another factor of –1 for each of the following criteria:
* `"auth_type": "Reversal"`
* `"transaction_type": "Merchant Credit"`
* `"transaction_type": "Payment"`

Amount fields may not display a numeric value for non-active cards. Instead, the string `"none"` could be displayed.

currency.description:
The currency code for the amounts, unless otherwise indicated. This is the currency of the cardholder account. ISO 4217 Numeric Currency Code. 3 digits.

Example: `"840"`

trans_amount.description:
Transaction amount. Full amount of the authorization request, including upcharges and fees and after any currency conversion is performed.

Example: `"12.40"`

partial_amount.description:
If `partial_supported: true` and `response_code` is `10` or `87`, this is the amount of the partial approval.

Example: `"10.00"`

cashback_amount.description:
Cashback amount requested. This amount is included in `trans_amount`.

Example: `"5.00"`

fee_amount.description:
Amount of any fees. This amount is included in `trans_amount`.

Example: `"1.50"`

available_funds.description: The card's available balance before this transaction is applied. If this authorization request is approved, the card's available balance is affected within a few milliseconds after the approval is sent to the network. Keep in mind that this is the available balance known to SoFi Tech Solutions—if you are the system of record for your program, refer to your records to determine whether the account has sufficient funds. Example: `100.00`

amt_til_limit.description:
Amount remaining before `nearest_limit` is reached.

Example: `502.80`

nearest_limit.description:
The name of the first limit that would be reached if a partial authorization or denied authorization is overridden via the `override_limit` field. This field is present only when the limit would be reached in overriding the authorization.

Example: `"PCL Daily Limit"`

local_currency.description:
ISO 4217 numeric currency code for `local_currency_amount`, which is the currency at the point of sale. 3 digits.

Example: `"124"`

local_currency_amount.description:
Amount of the request in the currency at the point of sale. Upcharges and fees are not included.

Example: `"21.00"`

settle_currency.description: ISO 4217 numeric currency code for `settlement_currency_amount`. To understand what a settlement currency is, see Multicurrency BINs. 3 digits. Example: `"978"`

settle_currency_amount.description:
Amount of the request in the settlement currency. Upcharges and fees are not included.


Example: `"17.00"`

billing_currency.description:
ISO 4217 numeric currency code for `billing_currency_amount`.

Example: `840`

billing_currency_amount.description:
The amount of the transaction in the billing currency, which is the currency of the card account.

Example: `"12.40"`

local_surcharge_amt.description:
The surcharge amount in the currency at the point of sale.

Example: `"0.50"`

settle_surcharge_amt.description:
The surcharge amount in the settlement currency.

Example: `"0.75"`

settle_exchange_rate.description:
The factor used to convert from the local request amount to the settlement amount. The string has the pattern `<shift digit><exchange rate digits>`. The first digit specifies how many places from the right the decimal is moved. For example, `69985022` translates to an exchange rate of 9.985022%.

Example: `"69985022"`

exchange_rate.description:
The factor used to convert from the local request amount to the billing amount. The string has the pattern `<shift digit><exchange rate digits>`. The first digit specifies how many places from the right the decimal is moved. For example, `69985022` translates to an exchange rate of 9.985022%.

Example: `"65991234"`

upcharge_amount.description:
The upcharge amount, which is included in `trans_amount`.

Example: `"75.00"`

mcc.description:
Merchant category code. This value does not include leading zeros.

Example: `5992`

digital_commerce_data.description: _Mastercard only_. Contains data regarding a digital commerce transaction. Derived from DE048SE48. See Digital Commerce Solutions Indicators for more information.

entity_type_name.description:
SF3. The check-in entity type and entity name.

Example: `"202010030220"`

domain_id.description:
SF1. The entity responsible for populating the other fields in this object.

Example: `"01"`

program_id.description:
SF2. The specific digital commerce program.
          

Example: `"01"`

checkin_method.description:
SF4. The methods that a check-in entity applies to validate cardholder presence. **Required** when `program_id: 04`.

Example: `" "`

terminal_id.description:
The ID for the device that acquired the card information.

Example: `"A1Z23B99"`

merchant_id.description:
The merchant ID, as assigned by the network.

Example: `"39AJKEO30634KVN3"`

merchant_description.description:
The merchant description.

Example: `"123 WIDGETS MERCHANT BEVERLY HILLS CA"`

merchant_country.description:
ISO 3166-1 country code for the country where the merchant is located. 3 digits.

Example: `"840"`

merchant_postal_code.description:
Postal code, nine characters. Left-justified and padded with zeros. If there are nine zeros, then no postal code was provided.

Example: `"902100000"`

merchant_state.description:
Two-letter state or provincial designator for the merchant's location.

Example: `"NV"`

terminal_network.description:
Network to which the terminal belongs, Possible values are `VPA` (Visa PLUS Alliance), `Allpoint`, or `None` (another network). If you are not configured to receive this data, the value will always be `None`.


Example: `"VPA"`

mti.description: Message-type indicator, as defined by ISO 8583. See Message types in the _Authorization Controller API_ guide. Example: `"0200"`

recurring.description:
Whether a transaction is recurring: `Y` or `N`.

Example: `"N"`

cardholder_present.description:
Whether the physical card was present at the point of sale: `Y` or `N`.

Example: `"Y"`

transaction_initiator_code.description: *Mastercard only.* Whether the transaction was initiated by the cardholder or the merchant. Populated only when DE048 subfield 22 is present in the authorization request. See CIT and MIT Indicators for more information. Example: `"M101"`

is_advance_payment.description: _Visa only_. Field 126 SE 13. Whether the transaction is an advance payment, meaning that the merchant secures the payment before the goods or services are available.

cvv1.description:
Result of <<glossary:CVV>>1 validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

cvv2.description:
Result of CVV2 validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

cvv3.description:
Result of CVV3 validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

pin.description:
Result of PIN validation. Possible values:
* `Y` — Verified
* `F` — Failed
* `L` — Locked
* `M` — PIN not set
* `B` — Blocked
* `N` — No PIN was passed

arqc.description:
Result of validating the authorization request cryptogram for an EMV chip. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

offline_pin.description:
Result of validating the offline PIN. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present
* `E` — Offline PIN attempts exceeded
* `P` — Ignored due to risk params

avs_result.description: Result of the <> check. See AVS Codes for valid values. Example: `"Y"`

aav.description:
Result of validating the <<glossary:AAV>>/<<glossary:CAVV>>. Possible values:
* `Y` — Validated
* `F` — Failed
* `N` — Not present

avs_data.description: When the authorization includes an <<glossary:AVS>> request, this object contains the data that SoFi Tech Solutions used to calculate the AVS response.

zip.description:
Postal code provided by the cardholder.

Example: `"84121"`

address.description:
Numbers in the first address line, provided by the cardholder.

Example: `"1235"`

international.description: Whether this is an international transaction.

response_code.description: Authorization response code, which specifies whether a transaction is approved or denied. See the Authorization Response Codes enumeration for possible values. Example: `"05"`

auth_id.description: System-generated ID for the authorization. Use this ID to track the transaction throughout the system. For an explanation of how these IDs are generated, see Authorization identifiers in the _Transaction IDs_ guide. Example: `13371854`

partial_supported.description: Whether the merchant supports partial authorizations.

stip.description: This object is present when a <> transaction is processed by the network. See Stand-in processing in the _Authorization Controller API_ guide for more information.

detail.description: Advice reason code relayed from the network, which provides information on the STIP transaction. See Advice Reason Codes for valid values. Example: `"4000000"` or `"9020"`

stip_decision.description: The Authorization Response Code that was returned to the merchant by the STIP process. Example: `"00"`

additional_detail.description: More information about the STIP transaction. See STIP Additional Detail for valid values. Example: `"000003"`

is_stip_denial.description:
Whether the transaction was denied by the STIP process: `N` (approved). Denied STIP transactions do not trigger an Auth API message.

Example: `"N"`

incremental_auth.description: If this authorization is part of an an incremental sequence, this field is `true` and `original_id` contains the `auth_id` of the previous authorization in the sequence.

entry_type.description: Method of entering the <>, also known as <> entry mode. See DE022 Codes to correlate with the numerical values. Possible values: * `Card Not Present` — Online, mail order or telephone order * `Card On File` — _Mastercard only._ Card number is kept on file * `E-Commerce` — _Mastercard only._ The card was used on an ecommerce site * `EMV Chip` — The card has an EMV chip that was inserted in an EMV slot * `EMV Contactless` — Contactless transaction with EMV chip card * `EMV Fallback` — Unable to use the EMV chip: fallback to magstripe * `Magnetic Stripe` — The magnetic stripe was read * `Contactless` — Contactless transaction with magstripe card * `Manual` — Manually entered information * `Other` — None of the above

pin_entry_capability.description: Condition of the PIN pad at the point of sale. See DE022 Codes to correlate with the numerical values. Possible values: * `Capable` — Terminal has PIN-entry capability * `Incapable` — Terminal has no PIN-entry capability * `Inoperative` — Terminal has PIN-entry capability but it is not working * `Other` — Unknown PIN-entry capability, or not applicable.

payment_info.description: When `transaction_type` is `Payment`, the name of the sender and fund source, if provided in the request.

sender_name.description:
Name of the sender of the payment.

Example: `"John Doe"`.

fund_source.description:
Source of the payment.

Example: `"Visa Prepaid"`.

original_id.description:
The `auth_id` of a previous authorization that is linked to this authorization. For reversals or completions, this is the `auth_id` of the authorization that is being reversed or completed. For incremental sequences, this is the `auth_id` of the previous authorization in the sequence.

Example: `13663253`

risk_score.description:
The risk score provided by the network. Mastercard range: 0–999, Visa range: 01–99. Higher values indicate higher risk. Product settings determine whether the threshold was exceeded.

Example: `"23"`

token_type.description:
If this is a tokenized transaction, its type. Possible values:
* `Apple Inc`
* `Google Inc.`
* `Masterpass`
* `Merchant`
* `Microsoft`
* `Samsung Corporation`
* `Visa Checkout`

rules_denied.description:
Valid only when using our fraud-rules engine. List of fraud rules that caused a decline. Set the RULAP product parameter to receive these rules.

Example: `["hr_crypto:DENY", "intl_cnp_ecom:DENY"]`

rules_warned.description:
Valid only when using our fraud-rules engine. List of fraud rules that caused a warning. Set the RULAP product parameter to receive these rules.

Example: `["dom_cp:WARN"]`

bai.description: Business application identifier. _Visa only._ See the Business Application Identifier enumeration for possible values. Example: `"FD"`

risk_code.description:
_Mastercard only_. Fraud reason code. Indicates the key factors that influenced the value in `risk_score`.

Example: `"58"`

ecommerce.description: This object contains information related to <> authentication, if the website supported 3DS. Included in this information is the result of validating the <> for Mastercard or the <> for Visa. For detailed information about these fields, refer to The ecommerce object in the _3-D Secure Access Control Server_ guide.

is_ecommerce.description: Whether the transaction took place on a website that supports 3DS.

raw_eci.description:
The electronic commerce indicator (ECI) that is sent in the authorization request.

Example: `"212"`

merchant_asserts_data_protection.description: Whether the merchant or acquirer claims that the connection between the ecommerce site and the cardholder was encrypted.

merchant_asserts_authentication_attempte.description: Whether the merchant or acquirer claims that 3DS authentication was attempted.

merchant_asserts_authenticated.description: Whether the merchant or acquirer claims that the 3DS authentication was successful.

merchant_authentication_assertions_valid.description: Validation results of the merchant's assertions.

cavv_result_code.description: _Visa only_. A code that indicates the outcome of CAVV validation. See CAVV Result Code for valid values. Example: `"B"`

eligible_for_balance_return.description: Whether the cardholder's balance can be returned. This field is always `true` when `transaction_type: Balance Inquiry`. See Balance-inquiry responses in the _Authorization Controller API_ guide for information on returning balances in the response to this message.

emv.description: Additional EMV information. Also see EMV entry types under `entry_type` and EMV-related fields under `validation_results`.

is_emv.description: This field is `true` if the `entry_type` is `EMV Chip` or `EMV Contactless`. When this value is `true`, the remaining fields below will be present, although they may be only partially populated, depending on the card network or EMV entry type.

brand.description:
Type of EMV. Possible values:
* `visa`
* `mastercard`
* `discover`

The card network may not match the EMV brand. For example, Visa EMV technology can be used on a card whose BIN is serviced through Allpoint.

terminal_verification_results.description:
This object interprets the status bits sent by the payment terminal, based on what happened during the transaction, such as whether the cardholder entered a valid PIN. Selected bits of the TVR have been separated out into the Boolean fields below.

Use these fields with caution: There can be inconsistencies between different networks, and some bits are not applicable for certain entry types such as `EMV Contactless`. For example, Discover states that byte 3, bits 4 and 5 should be ignored for contactless transactions.

raw.description:
The raw TVR (as a hex string) that was received in the ISO 8583 message, if present. If not present this field is null and the remaining fields in the `terminal_verification_results` object will not be present.

Example: `"0000000000"`

online_pin_entered.description: _Byte 3, bit 3._ Whether a PIN is being sent in the ISO message for validation instead of using offline validation (where the EMV chip on the card validates the PIN).

pin_required_pad_pres_but_no_pin_entered.description: _Byte 3, bit 4._ Whether the merchant or cardholder chose to bypass PIN entry, and the PIN pad was operational.

pin_required_no_pad_or_bad_pad.description: _Byte 3, bit 5._ Whether a PIN was required but there was no PIN pad, or the PIN pad wasn't working.

pin_try_limit_exceeded.description: _Byte 3, bit 6._ Whether the PIN-try limit was exceeded. For example, the terminal read the PIN-try counter on the chip and it was zero.

cardholder_verification_not_successful.description: _Byte 3, bit 8._ Whether the terminal indicates that cardholder verification was not successful.

version.description:
Auth API version of this webhook.

Example: `"3.0"`

iias_info.description: _Visa only_. Present when the items or services being purchased include eligible medical expenses. Derived from Field 54 and Field 62. This object is present only when <> information is included with the authorization request. For more information, see IIAS fields in the _Auth API Field Detail_ guide.

iias_indicator.description:
`M` indicates that the card is an <<glossary:FSA>>, <<glossary:HRA>>, or <<glossary:HSA>> card. Field 62.4.

Example: `"M"`

merchant_verification_value.description:
IIAS merchant verification value for the <<glossary:SIGIS>>-certified merchant location. Field 62.20.

Example: `"1234560000"`

qualified_healthcare_products_total.description:
Amount of `trans_amount` that qualifies as a healthcare product or service. Field 54, amount type 4S.

Example: `"64.87"`

rx_total.description:
Amount that is prescription medication. Field 54, amount type 4U.

Example: `"64.87"`

vision_total.description:
Amount that is vision-related. Field 54, amount type 4V.

Example: `"0.00"`

clinic_total.description:
Amount that is a clinic visit. Field 54, amount type 4W.

Example: `"0.00"`

dental_total.description:
Amount that is dental-related. Field 54, amount type 4X.

Example: `"0.00"`

advanced_auth_api_fields.description: Selected subfields parsed from the ISO 8583 message. These fields are sent only when ADVAF is set and only by arrangement with SoFi Tech Solutions. See Advanced Auth API Fields for more information. Example: `"advanced_auth_api_fields": {"61": {"subfield 1": , "subfield 2": }}`

tar_info.description: Tokenization authorization request (TAR) data is provided by the network during mobile wallet provisioning. The following are the subfields in a tokenization authorization request. Note the distinctions between Mastercard and Visa networks. For enhanced provisioning security based on some of these fields, see Enhanced provisioning security in _Setup for Mobile Wallets_. If you do not receive this data for provisioning approved BINs, contact SoFi Tech Solutions for assistance.

correlation_id.description:
_Mastercard only._ Identifier assigned that can be used by the issuer to associate related tokenization requests and notification messages. 14 alphanumeric characters.

Example: `"D0002688797932"`

pan_source.description:
For Mastercard, this field identifies the method by which the cardholder is attempting to tokenize a PAN.
- `1` — Card on file
- `2` — Card added manually
- `3` — Card added via application


For Visa, this tag, if present, identifies whether it’s push provisioning.
- `01` — Key entered
- `02` — On file
- `03` — Mobile banking application
- `04` — Token
- `05` — Chip dip
- `06` — Contactless

If the value is `03`, then it is push provisioning.

payment_app_instance_id.description:
_Mastercard only._ Identifier associated with the payment application instance installed onto the customer's device. 48 alphanumeric characters.

Example: `"tSnaYXYaTSkz7DoGPz_wvVLhieie4lyhMPuMrvXx4kdAwkgV"`

device_ip.description:
For Mastercard, this field is the variable-length IP address. Each octet of the IP address is converted to hex and joined into one string, with the order maintained. 8 alphanumeric characters.

Example: `"83BF5B74"`

For Visa, this field contains the IP address of the device at the time of the provisioning request. 15 characters maximum.

Example: `"255.255.255.255"`

acc_id_hash.description:
_Mastercard only._ Contains the customer’s account ID associated with the wallet provider as a PBKDF2 hash. This account ID is typically the email address. The PBKDF2 function is performed using 10 iterations, a salt, and the lowercase account ID as the password. The salt is calculated by taking the lowercase UTF-8 bytes from the account ID and performing a SHA-256 hash operation.

**Example**:
Input (Password): `csharp@walletprovider.com`
Salt: `"41404d1bca85ddb59ab21466e277ac1ac5f61470be120c82a21b1e45b5248123"`
Count: `10`
Output: `"7098014b646d44c6f3b454c5d54f7a32b3b46e2b0c8e2367f3e5307e3036dfe6"`

cardholder_name.description:
_Mastercard only._ Contains the name of the cardholder. The format is represented in one of these two formats:
- LASTNAME/FIRSTNAME with the names delimited by a slash `/`.

Example: `"SMITH/JOE"`
- FIRSTNAME LASTNAME.

Example: `"JOE SMITH"`

27 characters maximum. If the cardholder’s name is longer than 27 positions, the data is truncated.

tokenization_recommendation.description:
The tokenization decision suggested by the wallet provider.

For Mastercard, possible values are:
- `0` — Decline
- `1` — Approve
- `2` — Requires additional authentication

For Visa, possible values are:
- `0` — Unconditionally approved
- `1` — Conditionally approved with further cardholder verification
- `2` — Not approved

tokenization_recommendation_standard_ver.description:
The version of the standards the wallet provider is using to determine the suggested tokenization recommendation.

- For Mastercard, this value is 2 digits.

Example: `"01"`
- For Visa, this value is a decimal value.

Example: `"0002.00"`

device_score.description:
The score assigned by the wallet provider for the device. The score is returned as a value between `1` and `5`, with `5` being most trusted.

Example: `5`

account_score.description:
_Mastercard only._ Score assigned by the wallet provider for the <<glossary:PAN>>. Value between`1` and `5`, with `5` being most trusted.

Example: `5`

active_tokens.description:
_Mastercard only._ Number of existing, active tokens for the PAN, excluding card-on-file tokens. Space-filled when the requested token is digitized to a server.

Example: `"08"`

tokenization_recommendation_reason_code.description: Indicates the specific reason the wallet provider is suggesting the tokenization recommendation. For Mastercard, the data of this field is a hex-encoded bitmap, whereby each bit corresponds to a specific reason code. If the wallet provider returns no reason, this field will contain spaces. See the possible values for Visa in the Tokenization Recommendation Reason Codes. Example: `"008011"`

tokenization_recommendation_reason_codes.description: _Mastercard only._ Indicates the specific reason the wallet provider is suggesting the tokenization recommendation. This field shows the interpretation of the hex-encoded bitmap in the `tokenization_recommendation_reason_code` field for Mastercard. See the possible values for this field in the Tokenization Recommendation Reason Codes. Example: `"08" `

location.description:
Latitude and longitude points where the cardholder's device was located at the time the tokenization was attempted.

- For Mastercard. The decimal latitude and longitude values, converted to hexadecimal.

Example: `"2F197A2E1"`
- For Visa, when available, the latitude and longitude points are provided with up to 4 digits of precision or rounded to a less-granular level.

Example: `"+39.13/-77.55"`

last_four_digits.description:
_Mastercard only._ Last four digits of the cardholder's mobile phone number associated with the active wallet.

Example: `"0885"`

token_type.description:
The type of requested token.
- `C` — Mastercard cloud-based payments
- `F` — Card on file
- `S` — Embedded secure element
- `H` — <<glossary:VTS>> cloud token

consumer_identifier.description: _Mastercard only._ Unique identifier for each cardholder, which must be verified by the financial institution before a cardholder can add their credentials to the payment-enabled device. Default: blank.

device_type.description:
_Visa only._ Device type value.
- `00` — Unknown
- `01` — Mobile phone
- `02` — Tablet
- `03` — Watch
- `04` — Mobile phone or tablet
- `05` — Personal computer

device_language.description:
_Visa only._ Language used by the cardholder’s device. 3 characters maximum.

Example: `"eng"` for English.

device_id.description:
_Visa only._ The device ID. 48 characters maximum.

Example: `"MTgwOTIxMTQzMjAwMTA0LUh0"`

device_number.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the device number, or the full or partial telephone number, when available. Provided by the Visa network.

Example: `"15127717396"`

device_name.description:
_Visa only._ The name of the device given by the cardholder. 16 characters maximum. Value is truncated when longer than maximum length.

Example: `"Work Phone"`

account_id.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the wallet account ID.

Example: `"eg2t6TyJQ2G8NIraaCypzg"`

account_email_addr.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the hashed full email address for the cardholder account that was sent by the wallet provider.

Example: `"\xc1_\xf8\xc8_/\xd1%%\x06\xc4?_"`

visa_token_score.description:
_Visa only._ Contains the Visa Token Score associated with a token. Scores range from 01-99, with higher values indicating higher risk. `00` indicates a token was not scored.
Example: `"01"`

fleet_info.description: Information that is provided for cards with fleet-card BINs, which are Mastercard only. See Fleet Cards for more information.

fleet_prompt_data.description:
Contains occurrences of the prompt code read from a card chip. There can be up to 5 prompt codes. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for the full list.

Example: `002` (vehicle number)

merchant_override_indicator.description: Indicates if the merchant point-of-sale supports the fleet spend control override capability: `0` (does not support) or `1` (supports)

control_override_items.description: Provides merchants with information, on a transaction basis, to override purchase restrictions to allow products to be purchased that may not have otherwise been allowed. Only to be populated when DE106SE2 contains the value `1`, indicating that the merchant point-of-sale supports the fleet spend-control override capability.

fuel_info.description:
Contains item-level detail information of the motor fuel product(s) purchased at the POS (3 digit code). Can have up to 3 subfields. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for the full list.

Example: `036` (racing fuel)

non_fuel_info.description:
Contains item-level detail information of the non-fuel product(s) purchased at the POS. Can have up to 12 subfields. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for the full list.

Example: `102` (car wash)

aifi_fields.description: _Colombia only_. Information related to ATM issuer-fee inquiries.

issuer_fee_inquiry_indicator.description: Contains `"01"` to indicate issuer-fee inquiry request. DE112SE035.

pos_transaction_status.description: Contains `"8"` to indicate account-status inquiry (ASI) service. DE061SF7.

issuer_fee_amt.description:
Amount of the ATD (domestic ATM) fee. This amount is displayed to the cardholder as the issuer fee. DE112SE036.

Example: `"15000.00"`

merchant_advice_code.description: _Mastercard only._ Contains the supported merchant advice code (MAC), if applicable: `03`, `40`, `41`, or `43`. The GMACD parameter must be set to `Y` to enable MAC decisioning.

fraud_results.description: _Mastercard only_. Contains the results from the Mastercard Fraud Rule Management Service. If you subscribe to this service, ask SoFi Tech Solutions to enable this object. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for DE048SE56 to interpret the values.

fraud_scoring_data.description: _Mastercard only._ DE048SE75. Contains the results from Mastercard's Expert Monitoring, Fraud Scoring Service, or Decision Intelligence (DI) service. If you subscribe to any of these services, ask SoFi Tech Solutions to enable this object. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for your service to interpret the values.

risk_assessment_score.description:
Mastercard Decision Intelligence (DI) score ranging from `0-999`.

Example: `"089"`

risk_assessment_score_reason_code.description:
