Fraud reason code. Indicates the key factors that influenced the value in `risk_assessment_score`.

Example: `"64"`

real_time_fraud_score.description:
The Fraud Rule Manager Service provides the rule-adjusted score of `000-999`, where `000` indicates the least likely fraudulent transaction and `999` indicates the most likely fraudulent transaction.

Example: `"089"`

real_time_fraud_score_reason_code_1.description:
An alphanumeric reason code that identifies the data used to derive the `real_time_fraud_score`.

Example: `"64"`

real_time_fraud_score_reason_code_2.description:
An alphanumeric reason code that identifies the data used to derive the `real_time_fraud_score`.

Example: `"00"`

digital_payment_data.description: _Mastercard only._ DE104SE4. Contains the results from Mastercard's Token Authentication Framework (TAF) program. If you subscribe to Mastercard's Expert Monitoring, Fraud Scoring Service, or Decision Intelligence (DI) service, ask SoFi Tech Solutions to enable this object to use for decisioning. Consult the documentation from Mastercard on DE104 Subelement 004 to interpret the values.

digital_service_provider.description:
Identifies the entity that authenticated the transaction. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for a complete list of values for DE104SE4SF1.

Example: `"001005A0010"`

digital_authentication_data.description:
Confirms that the transaction was fully authenticated, and identifies the authentication method used. Consult the documentation from Mastercard for a complete list of values for DE104SE5SF1.

Example:`"0010054TRID00200500000"`

latest_incremental_id.description:
The `auth_id` of the previous authorization in an incremental sequence when `incremental_auth: true`. This field contains the same information as `original_id` and is present only by request.

Example: `13371854`

original_incremental_id.description:
The `auth_id` of the first authorization in an incremental sequence when `incremental_auth: true`. This field is present only by request.

Example: `13369203`

account_attack_intelligence_score.description:
_Visa only_. A score for <<glossary:CNP>> transactions to evaluate risk of enumeration attacks. Field 104, Dataset 5B, Tag 85. Valid values are `01-99` or null. Lower scores mean less risk.

Example: `"24"`

relay_resistance_protocol_data.description: _Mastercard only_. DE048SE71. For tokenized (mobile wallet), contactless transactions, this is information captured at the terminal related to the possibility of relay attacks. For valid values, see Relay Resistance Protocol Data.

on_behalf_service.description:
The type of service performed on the transaction.

Example: `"51"`

result_1.description:
The first result from the on-behalf service.

Example: `"A"`

result_2.description:
The second result from the on-behalf service, if any.

Example: `"K"`

service_processing_type.description: _Visa only_. Service processing type for scheduled, deferred <>s. See Service Processing Types for valid values. Field 104 Dataset 57 Tag 80. Example: `"03"`

managed_service_indicator.description:
Whether this is a managed-service transaction. Tag 82.

Example: `"Y"`

agreement_type.description:
The type of managed service that was provided for this transaction. Consult the documentation from Visa for valid values. Tag C1. Max 4 char.

Example: `"1234"`

is_in_person_tap_transaction.description: _Visa only_. Whether this is a direct in-person tap transaction. Applies only to <<glossary:OCT>>s and <<glossary:AFT>>s. Field 34.

vdcap_info.description: _Visa only_. <<glossary:VDCAP>> information from Field 34, Field 56, and Field 111.

authentication_program.description: Indicates which authentication solution or data-sharing solution was used to process the transaction. See VDCAP Info for valid values. Field 34 Dataset 01 Tag C0. Example: `"01"`

consumer_device_ip_address.description:
External IP address that is the device public IP address used by the 3DS requestor application when it connects to the 3DS requestor environment. Field 34 Dataset 01 Tag 92.

Example: `"172.16.22.52"`

applied_special_service.description:
Indicates whether the merchant has used the eligible authentication or data-sharing method and provided the required data elements. Visa sends `1` (<<glossary:VDCAP>>) if all the conditions are met. Field 111 Dataset 56 Tag 89.

Example: `"1"`

other_phone_number.description:
A phone number belonging to the cardholder. Field 56 Dataset 02 Tag 83. Max 16 char.

Example: `"8015552333"`

browser_ip_address.description:
3DS browser IP address. Field 34 Dataset 01 Tag 89.

Example `"10.0.45.66"`

other_email_address.description:
An email address belonging to the cardholder. Field 56 Dataset 02 Tag 86. Max 99 char.

Example: `"3dsuser@exampledomain.com"`

device_id.description:
Unique identifier associated with the cardholder device. Field 34 Dataset 06 Tag 86. Max 64 char.

Example: `"device000"`

credit_info.description: Contains information related to credit accounts.

credit_card_balance.description:
The outstanding balance on a credit account. This value can be interpreted as being accurate as of the `opentobuy_ts`.

Example: "-249.51"

opentobuy_ts.description:
Date and time when when the `credit_card_balance` was last captured. Format is YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.ssssss and timezone is always `MST`, which is Arizona time (GMT -0700).

Example: `"2025-03-17 14:06:50.243654"`

mastercard_transaction_id_data.description: _Mastercard only_. Derived from DE105, Multi-Use Transaction Identification Data. Contains the <<glossary:TLID>>, which is globally unique in a distributed environment and used as a single unique reference to perform matching and linking of all message activity

tlid.description: DE105SE1. Transaction link identifier. A unique ID that Mastercard generates for each original transaction. Example: `"aabb112233445566"`

economically_related_tlid.description: DE105SE2. The Mastercard-generated TLID from an economically related independent transaction that a customer retains and returns in subsequent economically related transactions.

lifecycle_tlid_validation_data.description: Data relative to the TLID lifecycle.

action_indicator.description:
DE105SE3SF1. Indicates whether Mastercard modified the `tlid`, either because the customer did not provide a TLID in a lifecycle-linking scenario, or the TLID was unmatched. Possible values:
- `1` — Mastercard populated `tlid` with the original message TLID. The customer did not submit a lifecycle message with a TLID, and so `customer_provided_tlid` will not be populated.
- `2` — Mastercard populated `tlid` with the original lifecycle message TLID. The customer submitted the lifecycle message with a TLID value that did not match the original message. Mastercard moved the customer-provided TLID value to `customer_provided_tlid`.
- `3` — Mastercard generated a new TLID value for `tlid`. Mastercard was unable to match this lifecycle message to any original message. If the customer submitted this transaction with a TLID value, Mastercard moved the customer-provided TLID value to `customer_provided_tlid`.

customer_provided_tlid.description: DE105SE3SF2. Contains the customer-provided TLID value from DE105SE1 (`tlid`) when Mastercard is unable to confirm the validity of that customer-provided TLID value.

200.description: Use the fields in this schema to respond with your decision plus any instructions for SoFi Tech Solutions.

response_code.description: Authorization response code, which specifies whether a transaction is approved or denied. See the Authorization Response Codes enumeration for possible values. Example: `"05"`

avs_response.description: Use this field to override `avs_result`, if you believe `avs_result` is wrong. See AVS Codes for valid values. Example: `"Y"`

override_limit.description: Use this field to override authorization limits, if permitted. If this field is `true` then any limits that would be reached are overridden. Example: `true`

partial_amount.description: If `response_code` indicates a partial approval (`10` or `87`), this is the partial amount to approve. Example: `5.00`

transfer_prn.description: If you want to perform a transfer to cover a lack of funds, this is the PRN of the account to supply the funds. Example: `"155200002717"`

transfer_amount.description: The amount to transfer from the `transfer_prn` to the cardholder account. Example: `20.00`

source_transfer_type.description: The transaction type for the adjustment on the source account in `transfer_prn`. Use the value that SoFi Tech Solutions supplied. Case sensitive. Default: `pc`. Example: `"lm"`

dest_transfer_type.description: The transaction type for the adjustment to the cardholder account. Use the value that SoFi Tech Solutions supplied. Case sensitive. Default: `PC` Example: `"LM"`

available_balance.description: If `eligible_for_balance_return: true` AND you hold the ledger for the card account, populate this field with the card account's available balance to spend _before_ the transaction is performed. Otherwise, SoFi Tech Solutions sends the balance it has in the response message. The amount should be in the account currency. (The card networks will perform currency conversion as needed.) Example: `250.00`

savings_balance.description: If `eligible_for_balance_return: true` AND you hold the ledger for the cardholder's savings account, populate this field with the savings account balance in the currency of the account. Otherwise, SoFi Tech Solutions sends the balance it has in the response message. Example: `4000.00`

available_credit.description: If `eligible_for_balance_return: true` AND you hold the ledger for the cardholder's credit account, populate this field with the credit limit remaining in the currency of the account. Otherwise, SoFi Tech Solutions sends the remaining limit it has in the response message. Example: `1500.00`

merchant_advice_code.description: *Mastercard only.* Use this field to override MAC decisioning, if permitted. Leave blank if you do not wish to override the SoFi Tech Solutions MAC decision. SoFi Tech Solutions reverts to the original decision if an invalid MAC is provided. The MACO product parameter must be set to `Y` to enable overrides.
